Ubuntu 25.10 and 26.04 LTS ship sudo-rs as the default `sudo`. It reads the same `/etc/sudoers`, but when it meets a line it does not support it prints a syntax error and skips the whole line, so a rule that worked before the upgrade can quietly stop granting access. This release adds a check for that.

What is new in 0.4.0

- `sudodrift sudors-check` reads `/etc/sudoers` and every file it includes, and lists each line that sudo-rs rejects, ignores or handles differently. Each finding has a level (breaks, differs or info), the file and line, a short explanation, a suggested fix and a link to the sudo-rs source or doc it is based on.
- `--target ubuntu-26.04|ubuntu-25.10|upstream` picks which sudo-rs rules to check against. `--root DIR` checks a mounted image or a copy of `/etc`. `--format json` is there for scripts.
- Exit codes: 0 nothing at the `--fail-on` level (default breaks), 1 findings at that level or above, 2 error.
- `docs/sudo-rs.md` lists every rule with its source.

Example:

    sudo sudodrift sudors-check
    sudodrift sudors-check --root /mnt/image --fail-on differs

It only reads files and needs no network.

Known limits: aliases are not expanded, so a rejected `Cmnd_Alias` is reported on the alias line. The "breaks" results were checked against `visudo -c` from real sudo-rs builds (Ubuntu 26.04 and 25.10 packages, upstream 0.2.8, 0.2.13 and 0.2.15). The "differs" results come from reading the sudo-rs source and docs and were not tested by running commands through sudo-rs.

Install

    VER=v0.4.0; ARCH=amd64   # or arm64
    curl -fsSLO https://github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/releases/download/$VER/sudodrift_${VER#v}_linux_$ARCH.tar.gz
    curl -fsSLO https://github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/releases/download/$VER/SHA256SUMS
    sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
    tar xzf sudodrift_${VER#v}_linux_$ARCH.tar.gz
    sudo install -m 0755 sudodrift /usr/local/bin/

Or with Go: `go install github.com/sudodrift/sudodrift/cmd/sudodrift@v0.4.0`

The arm64 build was not run on arm64 hardware.
